source.title: Woven seagrass storage basket
source.description: Round woven seagrass storage basket, gently tapered so the rim is wider than the base, built from thick coiled seagrass rope in visible horizontal bands, with a chunky rolled rim and two woven cut-out side handles.
source.artDirection: Warm Japandi: natural seagrass in warm straw and pale oatmeal, matte unfinished fibre, no lining and no lid.

requestedSizeCm.note: Rough target for the demo catalogue. The recorded widthCm/depthCm/heightCm above are measured from the GLB and take precedence.

measured.method: backend/api/glb.py measure(), read back from the fitted GLB

knownLimitations: No real product: geometry, texture and proportions come from an AI-generated turnaround sheet, not from a manufacturer's model. matchType is generic_visual_proxy; do not present it as a specific purchasable item.
price_cents in the batch manifest is invented for the demo and has no vendor behind it.
The per-axis fit landed exactly on the requested 45 x 45 x 42 cm (residual 0.00 cm on every axis, anisotropy 5.52%), so no dimension was compromised.

Not visually inspected in a render. Verified geometrically from the GLB instead: the vertices in every horizontal slab from 30% to 99% of height sit entirely in the outer two tenths of the radius, and the top 15% of the model has zero vertices within half a radius of the axis — so the basket is genuinely open and hollow, with no lid, cap or filled interior.
It has a real closed woven floor, not an open-ended tube: a slab at y=0.84 cm contains vertices at every radius from the axis outward, while slabs above y=4 cm are wall-only.

Flat and stable on the floor: minY is exactly 0.0 cm and the contact band within 3 mm of the base spans a 32.7 x 32.7 cm disc (35.6 cm within 10 mm). That base disc is narrower than the 45 cm rim because the basket tapers, which matches the source sheet — placement logic keyed to the bounding-box footprint will reserve the rim's 45 cm, slightly more floor than the basket actually touches.

The woven surface is modelled as real displaced geometry rather than a normal map, so the base contact band fragments into many small clusters at millimetre resolution. It reads as a textured weave at room scale, not in close-up.

The source sheet's four views are a near-symmetric drum, so the three-quarter and rear views carried little extra information; fine detail around the handles is the generator's interpolation rather than observed from a distinct angle.
